subject: Plan options and portability details for PulseHealth - packaging & discounts
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@pulsehealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ops@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring Redwood for inference — packaging questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the intro call yesterday — quick follow-up with a few concrete asks so we can align internally on next steps.

Our main questions:
- Which plan (Hosted API vs Dedicated) makes sense for a multi-product rollout where we start with a conversational assistant (latency-sensitive) and add batch embeddings for analytics later?
- If we start on Hosted and later move to Dedicated, how disruptive is the migration and are there porting/compatibility guarantees?
- We have a mix of regulated PII flows and lower-sensitivity traffic. Is it reasonable to run the PII flows on Private/Dedicated while keeping the rest on Hosted under one agreement?
- Pricing: we expect ~10M tokens/month initially, growing to ~50M within 12 months. What discounts are typical for an annual commitment vs monthly? Are there bundling options (embed + generation) that reduce unit cost?

Procurement wants a short matrix of options (price for month-to-month, 12mo committed, and committed + Dedicated) and any portability caveats. Can you send a concise proposal we can take to procurement?

Thanks — Rajiv

Hi Rajiv — great questions, and I captured these for the procurement matrix you requested. Short answers up front: Hosted is the fastest path; Dedicated gives predictable latency and better isolation; migration is supported and we provide compatibility guidance and a runbook. You can absolutely mix Dedicated (for PII workloads) and Hosted (for lower-sensitivity traffic) under one commercial agreement — we call that a hybrid deployment.

I've attached a draft pricing matrix that outlines month-to-month vs 12mo committed pricing and a sample Dedicated uplift. Aditya — can you confirm the discount bands we can offer at 10M -> 50M token tiers and any promotional flexibility for PulseHealth? Dylan — please confirm the latency SLOs and a short note on migration effort for moving from Hosted -> Dedicated (preferably in bullet form).

Rajiv / Lena — I'll follow up with a clean final that you can share with Procurement (including a short mutual action plan).

Next steps I propose:

Vanessa — see notes below on pricing bands and negotiation room. I kept this short so you can forward a clean version to Rajiv.

Pricing bands (annual commitment, token-based model):
- 0–10M tokens/mo: list $0.020 / 1k tokens — typical small-account pricing
- 10M–30M tokens/mo: 15–18% off list depending on term (we can go to 18% for 12mo commit)
- 30M–100M tokens/mo: 20–28% off list; higher discounts tied to longer commit and minimum spend

Dedicated uplift: generally +30–45% on top of committed Hosted price for guaranteed capacity and isolation. If PulseHealth signs a multi-year Dedicated commit we can negotiate blended rates that smooth the uplift (proposal example in draft).

Bundling: we usually offer an embeddings + generation bundle that reduces the embeddings unit price by 25% when purchased with a generation commitment (applies to committed plans only). Seat/seat-like fees for console/monitoring are separate; include the first 5 seats in Enterprise package.

One-off credits: We're ok to offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10–15% of first-yr committed value for migration assistance (engineer hours, runbook, testing), conditioned on a 12mo commit. This is helpful to close deals.

Constraints / notes for Vanessa to relay:
- Procurement often wants month-to-month flexibility; price on month-to-month will be noticeably higher (typical reduction for annual is the negotiation lever).
- If they require on-prem air-gapped deployment the pricing model changes (capex / license-like) — call that out.

If you want, I can draft two clean tables (month-to-month vs 12mo vs Dedicated-commit) for tomorrow.

-Aditya

Quick tech note to include in the procurement packet (copyable into the mutual action plan):

- Migration effort (Hosted -> Dedicated): minimal model changes required; we provide a migration runbook and a 2-week validation window. Typical sequencing: staging on Dedicated small pool -> traffic mirroring -> gradual cutover. Plan for 1–2 weeks of SRE support from our side for the first rollout.
- Hybrid pattern: route PII traffic to a Dedicated pool deployed in their VPC (Private option) and keep non-PII on Redwood Hosted. SDK/API layer is the same; routing is a policy change — no code rewrite required.
- Performance: Dedicated with our medium GPU shape gives consistent 95th percentile latency under 150ms for short conversational prompts (<= 256 tokens); exact numbers depend on model.
- Cost-control levers: prefix KV caching for session assistants, batching for batch embed jobs; recommend enabling both to reduce token burn.

I've attached a short technical footprint doc you can share with their infra team.

-Dylan

Subject: PulseHealth packaging proposal — recommended path and next steps

Hi Rajiv / Lena — thanks for the quick turnaround internally. Attached is the clean packet for procurement:
- pricing-summary-final.xlsx (3 columns: month-to-month, 12mo committed, 12mo + Dedicated uplift)
- pulsehealth-mop.pdf (one-page mutual action plan with milestones and responsibilities)
- technical-footprint.pdf (for infra)

Summary recommendation (short):
- Start: Hosted API on a 12mo committed plan at the 10M token tier to secure a meaningful discount and onboarding credit.
- Parallel: Provision a Dedicated pool scoped to PII workloads on a 12mo commit; initial Dedicated capacity sized for peak conversational traffic and validated in a 2-week staging window.
- Portability: We guarantee API compatibility and provide a migration runbook for Hosted -> Dedicated; we include two weeks of SRE support for the migration as part of the onboarding credit proposal.
- Pricing mechanics: bundled embeddings discount (25%) applies if embedding usage exceeds 2M requests/month; onboarding credit available conditional on 12mo commitment.

Commercial ask / next step: please confirm which column Procurement prefers (month-to-month / 12mo committed / 12mo + Dedicated) and I will circulate a DocuSign to the procurement mailbox. If you want, we can also prepare a short procurement-friendly statement of work for the Dedicated deployment.
